title: Excess Flood Rate Manual: Base Rates, Flood Zone Factors and Tier Charges
content:
This rate manual page carries the rating figures of **Excess Flood Policies (Surplus Lines)** for every tier: the annual rate per 1,000 US dollars of excess dwelling limit and of excess personal property limit, the rating factor by FEMA flood zone, the elevation credit and its threshold, the flat annual charge for loss-of-use coverage, and the lowest annual premium after factors and credits, before fee and taxes.

## Tier rates and charges (US dollars)

| Tier | Excess Flood 250K | Excess Flood 500K | Excess Flood 1M | Excess Flood 2M | Excess Flood 3M | Excess Flood 5M |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Annual rate per 1,000 of excess dwelling limit | 1.85 | 1.55 | 1.3 | 1.1 | 0.95 | 0.82 |
| Annual rate per 1,000 of excess personal property limit | 2.1 | 1.85 | 1.6 | 1.4 | 1.25 | 1.1 |
| Flat annual charge for loss-of-use coverage | 60 | 110 | 150 | 210 | 300 | 450 |
| Lowest annual premium after factors and credits, before fee and taxes | 395 | 650 | 950 | 1450 | 2100 | 3250 |
| Lowest floor height above base flood elevation that earns the elevation credit, whole feet | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| Elevation credit when an accepted certificate shows that height or more, percent | 15 | 15 | 15 | 15 | 15 | 15 |

## Zone factor table (identical on every tier)

| FEMA flood zone | Rating factor |
|---|---|
| X, B, C | 0.3 |
| A99, AR | 0.6 |
| AO | 0.9 |
| A, AE, AH | 1.0 |
| D | 1.2 |
| V, VE | 2.75 |

## Reading the elevation credit threshold

The credit threshold is a floor height in whole feet above the base flood elevation. A certificate showing 2 whole feet or more meets it; one showing 1 whole foot, or a floor at or below the base flood elevation, does not.
